import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Particular values of the Riemann zeta function

*Reference:* [Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Particular_values_of_the_Riemann_zeta_function)
-/

namespace RiemannZetaValues

/--
$\zeta(5)$ is irrational.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 11 33]
theorem irrational_five : ∃ x, Irrational x ∧ riemannZeta 5 = x := by
  sorry

/--
$\zeta(7)$ is irrational.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 11 33]
theorem irrational_seven : ∃ x, Irrational x ∧ riemannZeta 7 = x := by
  sorry

/--
$\zeta(9)$ is irrational.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 11 33]
theorem irrational_nine : ∃ x, Irrational x ∧ riemannZeta 9 = x := by
  sorry

/--
$\zeta(11)$ is irrational.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 11 33]
theorem irrational_eleven : ∃ x, Irrational x ∧ riemannZeta 11 = x := by
  sorry

/--
$\zeta(2n + 1)$ is irrational for any $n\in\mathbb{N}^{+}$.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 11 33]
theorem irrational_odd (n : ℕ) (hn : 0 < n) :
    ∃ x, Irrational x ∧ riemannZeta (2 * n + 1) = x := by
  sorry

/--
$\zeta(3)$ is irrational.

[Ap79] Apéry, R. (1979). _Irrationalité de ζ(2) et ζ(3)_. Astérisque. 61: 11–13.
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 11 33]
theorem irrational_three : ∃ x, Irrational x ∧ riemannZeta 3 = x := by
  sorry

/--
There are infinitely many $\zeta(2n + 1)$, $n \in \mathbb{N}$, that are irrational.

[Ri00] Rivoal, T. (2000). _La fonction zeta de Riemann prend une infinité de valeurs irrationnelles aux entiers impairs_. Comptes Rendus de l'Académie des Sciences, Série I. 331 (4): 267–270.
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 11 33]
theorem infinite_irrational_at_odd :
    { n : ℕ | ∃ x, Irrational x ∧ riemannZeta (2 * n + 1) = x }.Infinite := by
  sorry

/--
At least one of $\zeta(5), \zeta(7), \zeta(9)$ or $\zeta(11)$ is irrational.

[Zu01]  W. Zudilin (2001). _One of the numbers ζ(5), ζ(7), ζ(9), ζ(11) is irrational_. Russ. Math. Surv. 56 (4): 774–776.
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 11 33]
theorem exists_irrational_of_five_seven_nine_eleven :
    {5, 7, 9, 11} ∩ { a | ∃ x, Irrational x ∧ riemannZeta a = x} |>.Nonempty := by
  sorry

end RiemannZetaValues

reformulations.difference: The Lean set allows n = 0, hence includes a test of Mathlib’s assigned value at ζ(1), whereas Rivoal’s introduction specifies ζ(2n+1) for integers n ≥ 1.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: Removing the index 0 changes the set by at most one element and therefore preserves infinitude, irrespective of the assigned value at ζ(1). For n > 0, ζ(2n+1) is real, and the existential irrational real witness is equivalent to irrationality of its real value. The exact equivalence to `{n : ℕ | 0 < n ∧ Irrational (riemannZeta (2 * n + 1)).re}.Infinite` is proved as `infinite_odd_positive_iff` in /workspace/review/scratch.lean, without using any sorry-backed theorem.

reformulations.difference: The source’s “at least one” assertion is expressed as nonemptiness of an intersection of sets of complex arguments, rather than as a four-way disjunction.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: An element of the intersection must equal 5, 7, 9, or 11 and satisfy the irrational-real-witness predicate. Each corresponding zeta value is real, so intersection nonemptiness is equivalent to `Irrational (riemannZeta 5).re ∨ Irrational (riemannZeta 7).re ∨ Irrational (riemannZeta 9).re ∨ Irrational (riemannZeta 11).re`. This exact equivalence is proved as `four_zeta_values_iff` in /workspace/review/scratch.lean, without sorry-backed premises.

sources_consulted: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Particular_values_of_the_Riemann_zeta_function — especially “Odd positive integers” and its references.
R. Apéry, “Irrationalité de ζ2 et ζ3,” Astérisque 61 (1979), 11–13: https://www.numdam.org/item/AST_1979__61__11_0.pdf

T. Rivoal, “La fonction zeta de Riemann prend une infinité de valeurs irrationnelles aux entiers impairs,” C. R. Acad. Sci. Paris, Série I 331 (2000), 267–270 — LaTeX abstract, introduction, and Theorem 1: https://arxiv.org/e-print/math/0008051

W. Zudilin, “One of the numbers ζ(5), ζ(7), ζ(9), ζ(11) is irrational,” Russian Mathematical Surveys 56 (2001), 774–776 — original English paper, read using OCR: https://www.math.ru.nl/~zudilin/PS/zeta5-11$.pdf
